review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its simp-tagged lemmas: antipodeAlgHom_apply, convCompMonoidHom_apply, the Point conversion lemmas, pointIncl_apply, pointInclLE_self, the pointsMk(Add)_pointIncl(LE) lemmas, toAlgHom_pointMap, pointsMap_pointsMkAdd and Points.smul_pointsMkAdd. I found no loops and no competing rules among them. I deliberately did not recommend @[simp] on toAlgHom_pointIncl. It shares a head with the simp lemma pointIncl_apply, so it could fire first on the unapplied subterm and compete with it. I grepped downstream P2M files to see how the lemmas are used. I could not run Lean, so the suggestions are untested. Whether Point.one_apply, whose right-hand side is algebraMap R L (counit a), is the best normal form is a judgement call, and I did not weigh it against Point.mul_apply, which expands into a lift of comul. Other non-simp rfl lemmas, such as toConv_mul and pointInclLE_succ_self, looked like intentional API with no clear simp benefit.

findings.excerpt: G.pointsMkAdd L v (Additive.ofMul x) = G.pointsMkAdd L v (Additive.ofMul y) ↔ x = y
findings.problem: This is an injectivity/cancellation iff. It turns an equality of images in the direct limit into an equality of level-v points, which is a strictly simpler goal. It is not tagged @[simp]. The file already makes the neighbouring lemmas pointsMkAdd_pointIncl and pointsMkAdd_pointInclLE simp, so simp can normalise pointsMkAdd terms but cannot cancel the outer pointsMkAdd on both sides of an equality. The file's own proof of pointsMap_injective_of_injective has to call this lemma by hand with `rw` twice (lines 401–402), after the simp lemmas have already done the other rewriting.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to pointsMkAdd_eq_pointsMkAdd_iff. Optionally add a companion iff for the multiplicative pointsMk, `pointsMk L v x = pointsMk L v y ↔ x = y`, stated via `(pointsMk_injective v).eq_iff`, and tag it `@[simp]` too. The lemma has a plain `x = y` right-hand side, so it cannot loop. Its left-hand side is a specific pattern with the same level v on both sides, so it should not interfere with other rules.
findings.benefit: Goals of the form `pointsMkAdd v (ofMul x) = pointsMkAdd v (ofMul y)` reduce automatically to `x = y`. This is especially useful after `pointsMap_pointsMkAdd` and `pointsMkAdd_pointInclLE` have rewritten both sides to the same level. Manual `rw` steps like the ones at lines 401–402 can then become `simp`.

findings.excerpt: theorem one_apply (a : G.level v) : toAlgHom (1 : G.Point L v) a = algebraMap R L (counit (R := R) a) := rfl
findings.problem: Point.one_apply is the canonical evaluation lemma for the unit point, but it has no @[simp] attribute. This is inconsistent with the other evaluation lemmas, `pointIncl_apply` and `toAlgHom_pointMap`, which are simp. Downstream files have to name it in every `simp only` call, together with `Point.toAlgHom_ofAlgHom` and `AlgHom.comp_apply`. As a result, `simp` cannot evaluate `toAlgHom 1 a`, which is neither unfolded nor otherwise simplified by default. It is also a different spelling from `Point.toConv_one`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `Point.one_apply` with `@[simp]`. Its right-hand side, `algebraMap R L (counit a)`, is the natural normal form and contains no `toAlgHom`, so it cannot loop. Leave `Point.mul_apply` non-simp, because its right-hand side expands into `Algebra.TensorProduct.lift … (comul a)`, which is an unwanted expansion by default. For `mul_apply`, keep the explicit `simp only` calls.
findings.benefit: The recurring `simp only [..., PDivisibleGroup.Point.one_apply]` call sites would shrink or become plain `simp`. Evaluating the identity point would also behave consistently with the other simp-evaluated point maps.
